chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension with prediabetes and anemia
history_of_present_illness: The 48-year-old male has persistent stage 2 hypertension (BP 148/106 mmHg) despite being on lisinopril 10 mg. He has a long-standing prediabetic state (A1c 6.8%) and chronic anemia diagnosed over 20 years ago. Severe anxiety/panic disorder and ongoing stress, exposure to violence, and low educational attainment contribute to poor disease self‑management. Chronic sinusitis remains active. No recent labs for lipids, renal function, or anemia work‑up are available, and no additional therapies for his metabolic or psychiatric conditions are documented.

active_problems.name: Reports of violence in the environment

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include part‑time employment (resolved 2022‑09‑07), gingivitis (resolved 2018‑09‑12 and 2016‑09‑07), full‑time employment (resolved 2020‑09‑02), viral sinusitis (resolved 2018‑01‑10), prior stress (resolved 2020‑09‑02), earlier reports of violence (resolved 2018‑08‑29), limited social contact (resolved 2018‑08‑29), and a medication review due (resolved 2016‑08‑24).
social_determinants: Stress, full‑time employment, ongoing exposure to violence, low educational attainment (primary school only), and limited health literacy likely affect adherence and lifestyle choices.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular: Stage 2 hypertension, prediabetes, anemia, and chronic anxiety place the patient at elevated risk for ischemic heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and peripheral vascular disease. Renal: Hypertension and lack of renal labs raise concern for chronic kidney disease. Metabolic: Prediabetes (A1c 6.8%) confers high risk of progression to type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome. Hematologic: Chronic anemia may worsen cardiac workload and could be related to CKD or iron deficiency. Neurologic: Vascular risk factors (HTN, prediabetes) increase risk for stroke and cognitive decline.

The current therapeutic regimen is insufficient, and key laboratory and lifestyle data are missing, indicating high cardiovascular and metabolic risk that requires comprehensive evaluation and intensified management.
